title: Article 134 — Appellate jurisdiction of Supreme Court in regard to criminal matters

content.overview: Article 134 provides for appeal to the Supreme Court from any judgment, final order or sentence of a High Court in the territory of India in a criminal proceeding: (a) if the High Court has on appeal reversed an order of acquittal of an accused person and sentenced him to death or to imprisonment for life or for a period of not less than ten years; (b) if the High Court has withdrawn for trial before itself any case from any court subordinate to its authority and has in such trial convicted the accused and sentenced him to death or to imprisonment for life or for a period of not less than ten years; or (c) if the High Court certifies under Article 134A that the case is a fit one for appeal to the Supreme Court. Parliament may by law confer further criminal appellate powers on the Supreme Court.
content.glance: Criminal appeal to SC: HC reverses acquittal and sentences to death/life/≥10 years; or HC withdraws and convicts with such sentence; or HC certifies fitness under Art 134A.
content.study:
Article 134 criminal appeals from High Courts:
(a) HC on appeal reverses acquittal and sentences to death, life imprisonment, or ≥10 years.
(b) HC withdraws case from subordinate court, tries, convicts, and sentences to death, life, or ≥10 years.
(c) HC certifies under Art 134A that the case is fit for appeal to the SC.

Parliament may enlarge criminal appellate jurisdiction by law.

Examination: three pathways; sentence thresholds in (a)/(b); certificate pathway (c); parliamentary enlargement.

sections.heading: Three pathways
sections.body:
1. HC reverses acquittal on appeal and sentences to death / life / ≥10 years.
2. HC withdraws, tries, convicts, and sentences to death / life / ≥10 years.
3. HC certifies fitness for appeal under Art 134A.
Parliament may confer further criminal appellate powers by law.

questionsAndAnswers.question: When does a criminal appeal lie to the Supreme Court under Article 134?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 134, an appeal lies to the Supreme Court from a High Court in a criminal proceeding if (a) the High Court has on appeal reversed an order of acquittal and sentenced the accused to death, imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for not less than ten years; or (b) the High Court has withdrawn a case for trial before itself, convicted the accused, and imposed such a sentence; or (c) the High Court certifies under Article 134A that the case is a fit one for appeal to the Supreme Court. Parliament may by law confer further powers on the Supreme Court to entertain criminal appeals.

examTips: Reverse acquittal + death/life/≥10 yrs; withdraw-and-convict + same; or fitness certificate.

keyTakeaways: Art 134: criminal appellate jurisdiction — specified sentence pathways and certificate.
